In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exfoliation process is not caused by the lens but is a ciliary process.

the exfoliation material contains glycoconjugate(s) with galactose residues in the terminal nonreducing position, and with galactosamine and N-acetyl-galactosamine residues, and that these glycoconjug-ate(s) are produced in part by the nonpig-mented ciliary epithelial cells.
the etiopathology of exfoliation is not yet fully understood, and the results of the present study do not contribute to the elucidation of its pathogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exfoliation material is a complex glycoprotein with a high content of N-acetylglycosamine and galactose residues, and it may have a common origin with ciliary zonular proteins.
the nonpigmented epithelium of the ciliary process is a major source of exfoliation-related glycoprotein, which is also expressed in the zonular lamellae and fibers.

the lectin histochemistry of the ciliary epithelum and exfoliation material is similar and that the nonpigmented epithelium of the ciliary process seems to be a possible source of galactose-containing components in capsular glauma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lectin histochemistry is a valuable tool for the study of capsular glaucomas.
the lens capsule is never labeled by any of the lectins used in our study.
lectin histochemistry may provide useful information for the etiopathogenic studies of exfoliation glaucoma and the related exfoliation syndrome.
